title: "Stage 2 – R and Quarto"
case: europeanisation
bibliography: [../../references.bib, ../../references-new.bib]
---
The second stage is a first working session in R, then R on the country-year panel of the case study and the document format in which your case-study report is written. It ends with the paper of the original author (OA) and the first sections of the background page, and takes nearly six hours.

## 1. R on a first file

[Open Getting started with R at Reading the data](https://codemoreh.github.io/ar4ds/tools/r.html#sec-reading){.btn .btn-primary target="_blank"}

Work from [Reading the data](https://codemoreh.github.io/ar4ds/tools/r.html#sec-reading) to [A first figure](https://codemoreh.github.io/ar4ds/tools/r.html#sec-figure) in the module on the AR4DS site. Type each block rather than pasting it, into the blocks of the module, which run in your browser.

## 2. R on the panel of the case study {#r-on-the-panel-of-the-case}

[Open R on the country-year panel](../../companion/intro-r.qmd#sec-formats){.btn .btn-primary target="_blank"}

Work through [Other formats, and fetching data](../../companion/intro-r.qmd#sec-formats) and [The grammar of graphics](../../companion/intro-r.qmd#sec-grammar) in the module R on the country-year panel. Type the blocks into your workspace, which holds the panel, and keep a script of your own that reads `europeanisation_cy.csv` and draws the cosmopolitan framing of each country-year against its unemployment rate.

## 3. Quarto

[Open Quarto documents](https://codemoreh.github.io/ar4ds/tools/quarto.html#sec-what){.btn .btn-primary target="_blank"}

Work from [Source and output](https://codemoreh.github.io/ar4ds/tools/quarto.html#sec-what) to [Citations](https://codemoreh.github.io/ar4ds/tools/quarto.html#sec-citations) in the module on the AR4DS site. Write and render a Quarto document of your own that holds your figure, a cross-reference to it and a citation. Then render the report of your workspace, `index.qmd`, once, and read through the five tasks that you will fill in.

## 4. The paper

[Open the paper](https://doi.org/10.1093/esr/jcw008){.btn .btn-primary target="_blank"}

Read the whole article of the OA [@Teney2016DoesEUEconomic]. Follow the two hypotheses about economic crisis and the framing of the EU, the question on what the EU means to the respondent, the macro indicators and the multilevel models, and find the sentence from which SCORE took the claim.

## 5. Background {#the-case-study}

[Read the background](../../background.qmd){.btn .btn-primary target="_blank"}

Read sections 1 to 3 of the background page: [the original study](../../background.qmd#sec-study), [the SCORE programme](../../background.qmd#sec-score) and the SCORE robustness study [@AczelEtAl2026InvestigatingAnalyticalRobustness], and [the five reanalysts](../../background.qmd#sec-reanalysts). Then write the claim of the case study in your own words.

**Shortcuts.** If you already write R with the tidyverse, read the section on [the datawizard verbs](https://codemoreh.github.io/ar4ds/tools/r.html#sec-verbs) in Getting started with R, which the workshop materials use wherever they do the job, then the second step of this stage, and run the rest of the first step only where its output surprises you. If you already write Quarto, render the report of the workspace and move on.
